findings.issue: Urgent care leaves action timing/facility unclear for vomiting blood or unstoppable bleeding, particularly in English.
findings.action: Separate immediate emergency assessment for vomiting blood/major bleeding from prompt clinical advice for tarry stool; bind each action independently. Keep statin muscle symptoms as a separate item.

findings.issue: Single-source direct limits and incomplete explanation of myocardial injury versus infarction.
findings.action: Add an independently written serial-troponin/ECG limitation source; explain why injury marker alone is not cause diagnosis. NSTEMI must not mean only partial obstruction; current Mayo explicitly notes some total blockages.

findings.issue: Only benign mimics and stable angina described; urgent noncoronary causes and unstable angina are not developed.
findings.action: Explain dangerous alternatives such as aortic dissection and pulmonary embolism with actual source-supported clues and emergency action; symptom differences are not home exclusion tests.

findings.issue: Type/timing/availability compound not fully supported by the two cited generic pages.
findings.action: Read current ACS guideline sections and distinguish STEMI fibrinolysis context, bleeding exclusions and NSTE-ACS management without creating dosing or a universal pathway.

findings.issue: Medication goals are named but ACE/beta-blocker roles and relevant conditions are not explained; primary-prevention aspirin support was unbound.
findings.action: Separate major categories/representative names, benefit, limitations and consultation risks. Bind FDA/AHA aspirin risk material, disclosing common AHA group. Do not turn differing DAPT duration guidance into one universal duration.

findings.issue: Kidney dietary restrictions and pregnancy-specific care have limited direct independent support. Postpartum patients no longer have an in-utero fetus.
findings.action: Give condition-specific examples and population bounds, and independently verify pregnancy testing/treatment context; retain rapid emergency assessment.

findings.issue: Routine follow-up organization and symptom reporting attached to whole pages rather than every action.
findings.action: Bind actual discharge/follow-up materials and explain what to record. AHA2025 item9 supports region-specific lipid reassessment; do not copy thresholds without scope or counterpart.

findings.issue: Professional and patient summaries vary in detail; some simplifications conflict with more precise recommendations.
findings.action: Keep NHS/Mayo aspirin differences explicitly regional. Do not import unconditional oxygen from Mayo treatment paragraph; indexed JACC2025 section4.1 is hypoxia-conditioned. AHA patient STEMI/NSTEMI diagram must not override Mayo total-obstruction exception.

independence: All NHLBI pages one NIH writer group; all Mayo pages one group; NHS medicines/chest/MI one national writer group. Current AHA/ACC joint document and its summaries count once. Patient prose may rely on overlapping underlying guidelines; no independent-trial replication inferred.
mece: Parent MI entry must not count each STEMI/NSTEMI/site-specific or recurrent ICD leaf without explicit semantic adjudication. Chest-pain symptom entry remains linked rather than duplicated.
license: Original editorial assessments and URL/heading locators; no full source text redistributed.
bilingual_assessment: All42 Chinese/English paragraphs read side by side. No differing numeric thresholds in current body. Urgent-care English and postpartum fetal scope require clarification; no mechanical removal of negative limits.
